──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n333\t// Entry point\n334\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n335\t\n336\t/// Entry point called from `main`.\n337\tpub fn run() -> Result<()> {\n338\t    let cli = ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n398\t// Command handlers\n399\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n400\t\n401\t/// `needle run` — launch a worker.\n402\t///\n403\t/// Always creates dedicated tmux sessions for workers, even when invoked from\n404\t/// inside an existing tmux session. The only exception is a re-entrant inner\n405\t/// invocation launched by `launch_in_tmux()`, which is identified by the\n406\t/// `NEEDLE_INNER=1` environment variable and runs the worker directly.\n407\tfn cmd_run(\n408\t    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n409\t    agent: Option<String>,\n410\t    count: u32,\n411\t    identifier: Option<String>,\n412\t    timeout: Option<u64>,\n413\t    resume: bool,\n414\t    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n415\t) -> Result<()> {\n416\t    // Determine workspace root (CLI arg → canonicalized, else global default).\n417\t    let workspace_root = if let Some(ref ws) = workspace {\n418\t        ws.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| ws.clone())\n419\t    } else {\n420\t        let global = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n421\t        global.workspace.default.clone()\n422\t    };\n423\t\n424\t    // Load full resolved config (global → workspace .needle.yaml → env → CLI).\n425\t    let cli_overrides = CliOverrides {\n426\t        workspace: Some(workspace_root.clone()),\n427\t        agent_binary: agent.clone(),\n428\t        max_workers: None,\n429\t        ..Default::default()\n430\t    };\n431\t    let (mut config, _) = ConfigLoader::load_resolved(&workspace_root, cli_overrides)?;\n432\t\n433\t    if let Some(t) = timeout {\n434\t        config.agent.timeout = t;\n435\t    }\n436\t\n437\t    if let Some(hr) = hot_reload {\n438\t        config.self_modification.hot_reload = hr;\n439\t    }\n440\t\n441\t    if resume {\n442\t        // Hot-reload resume: inherit worker identity from --identifier,\n443\t        // load state from heartbeat file + registry, continue from SELECTING.\n444\t        let worker_id = identifier\n445\t            .clone()\n446\t            .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string());\n447\t\n448\t        // Load resume state from heartbeat and registry.\n449\t        let resume_state = crate::upgrade::ResumeState::load(&config, &worker_id)?;\n450\t\n451\t        // Emit upgrade.completed telemetry.\n452\t        let current_hash = crate::upgrade::file_hash(\n453\t            &std::env::current_exe().context(\"failed to locate own binary\")?,\n454\t        )\n455\t        .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"unknown\".to_string());\n456\t\n457\t        match &resume_state {\n458\t            Some(state) => {\n459\t                tracing::info!(\n460\t                    worker = %worker_id,\n461\t                    binary_hash = %&current_hash[..current_hash.len().min(12)],\n462\t                    beads_processed = state.beads_processed,\n463\t                    session = %state.session,\n464\t                    \"resuming worker after hot-reload\"\n465\t                );\n466\t            }\n467\t            None => {\n468\t                tracing::info!(\n469\t                    worker = %worker_id,\n470\t                    binary_hash = %&current_hash[..current_hash.len().min(12)],\n471\t                    \"resuming worker after hot-reload (no prior state found)\"\n472\t                );\n473\t            }\n474\t        }\n475\t\n476\t        let tel = crate::telemetry::Telemetry::from_config(worker_id.clone(), &config.telemetry)\n477\t            .unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n478\t                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"hook telemetry init failed, falling back\");\n479\t                crate::telemetry::Telemetry::new(worker_id.clone())\n480\t            });\n481\t        tel.emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::UpgradeCompleted {\n482\t            new_hash: current_hash,\n483\t        })?;\n484\t\n485\t        return run_worker(config, worker_id);\n486\t    }\n487\t\n488\t    if is_needle_inner() {\n489\t        // Re-entrant inner invocation launched by launch_in_tmux() — run\n490\t        // the worker directly inside the dedicated session already created.\n491\t        let worker_id = identifier\n492\t            .clone()\n493\t            .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string());\n494\t        let agent_name = agent.as_deref().unwrap_or(&config.agent.default);\n495\t        let session_name = sanitize_session_name(&format!(\"needle-{agent_name}-{worker_id}\"));\n496\t        tracing::info!(worker = %worker_id, session = %session_name, \"starting worker (inner re-entrant invocation)\");\n497\t        run_worker(config, worker_id)\n498\t    } else {\n499\t        // Always create dedicated tmux sessions, even if already inside tmux.\n500\t        launch_workers(\n501\t            config, workspace, agent, count, identifier, timeout, hot_reload,\n502\t        )\n503\t    }\n504\t}\n505\t\n506\t/// Launch `count` workers in separate tmux sessions with staggered startup delays.\n507\tfn launch_workers(\n508\t    config: Config,\n509\t    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n510\t    agent: Option<String>,\n511\t    count: u32,\n512\t    identifier: Option<String>,\n513\t    timeout: Option<u64>,\n514\t    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n515\t) -> Result<()> {\n516\t    let agent_name = agent\n517\t        .as_deref()\n518\t        .unwrap_or(&config.agent.default)\n519\t        .to_string();\n520\t    let stagger_secs = config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds;\n521\t    let max_workers = config.worker.max_workers;\n522\t\n523\t    if count == 0 {\n524\t        bail!(\"--count must be at least 1\");\n525\t    }\n526\t    if count as usize > NATO_ALPHABET.len() {\n527\t        bail!(\n528\t            \"--count {} exceeds the maximum of {} (NATO alphabet size)\",\n529\t            count,\n530\t            NATO_ALPHABET.len()\n531\t        );\n532\t    }\n533\t\n534\t    // Enforce max_workers cap (0 means unlimited).\n535\t    let effective_count = if max_workers > 0 && count > max_workers {\n536\t        tracing::warn!(\n537\t            requested = count,\n538\t            capped_to = max_workers,\n539\t            \"count exceeds max_workers; capping\"\n540\t        );\n541\t        eprintln!(\n542\t            \"Warning: --count {count} exceeds max_workers={max_workers}; launching {max_workers} workers\"\n543\t        );\n544\t        max_workers\n545\t    } else {\n546\t        count\n547\t    };\n548\t\n549\t    // --identifier is only meaningful for a single worker.\n550\t    if effective_count > 1 && identifier.is_some() {\n551\t        bail!(\"--identifier cannot be combined with --count > 1; identifiers are auto-assigned from the NATO alphabet\");\n552\t    }\n553\t\n554\t    // Detect existing sessions to avoid name collisions.\n555\t    let occupied = occupied_worker_ids(&agent_name)?;\n556\t    if !occupied.is_empty() {\n557\t        tracing::info!(\n558\t            occupied = ?occupied,\n559\t            \"found existing worker sessions\"\n560\t        );\n561\t    }\n562\t\n563\t    // Reject --identifier collision early.\n564\t    if let Some(ref id) = identifier {\n565\t        if occupied.contains(id) {\n566\t            bail!(\n567\t                \"worker '{}' is already running in session 'needle-{}-{}'\",\n568\t                id,\n569\t                agent_name,\n570\t                id\n571\t            );\n572\t        }\n573\t    }\n574\t\n575\t    // Build the list of worker IDs, skipping occupied names.\n576\t    let worker_ids: Vec<String> = if effective_count == 1 {\n577\t        vec![identifier.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {\n578\t            // Pick the first available NATO name.\n579\t            NATO_ALPHABET\n580\t                .iter()\n581\t                .find(|name| !occupied.contains(**name))\n582\t                .map(|s| s.to_string())\n583\t                .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string())\n584\t        })]\n585\t    } else {\n586\t        let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(effective_count as usize);\n587\t        for name in NATO_ALPHABET {\n588\t            if ids.len() >= effective_count as usize {\n589\t                break;\n590\t            }\n591\t            if occupied.contains(*name) {\n592\t                tracing::warn!(\n593\t                    worker_id = %name,\n594\t                    \"skipping occupied worker name\"\n595\t                );\n596\t                continue;\n597\t            }\n598\t            ids.push(name.to_string());\n599\t        }\n600\t        if ids.len() < effective_count as usize {\n601\t            bail!(\n602\t                \"cannot launch {} workers — only {} NATO names available ({} occupied)\",\n603\t                effective_count,\n604\t                ids.len(),\n605\t                occupied.len()\n606\t            );\n607\t        }\n608\t        ids\n609\t    };\n610\t\n611\t    for (seq, worker_id) in worker_ids.iter().enumerate() {\n612\t        let session_name = sanitize_session_name(&format!(\"needle-{agent_name}-{worker_id}\"));\n613\t\n614\t        tracing::info!(\n615\t            worker_id = %worker_id,\n616\t            sequence = seq,\n617\t            total = effective_count,\n618\t            session = %session_name,\n619\t            \"launching worker\"\n620\t        );\n621\t\n622\t        // Stagger: sleep before launching subsequent workers.\n623\t        if seq > 0 && stagger_secs > 0 {\n624\t            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(stagger_secs));\n625\t        }\n626\t\n627\t        launch_in_tmux(\n628\t            &session_name,\n629\t            workspace.clone(),\n630\t            agent.clone(),\n631\t            Some(worker_id.clone()),\n632\t            timeout,\n633\t            hot_reload,\n634\t        )?;\n635\t\n636\t        println!(\n637\t            \"[{}/{}] Started worker '{}' in tmux session: {session_name}\",\n638\t            seq + 1,\n639\t            effective_count,\n640\t            worker_id\n641\t        );\n642\t    }\n643\t\n644\t    let sanitized_agent = sanitize_session_name(&agent_name);\n645\t    if effective_count > 1 {\n646\t        println!(\n647\t            \"\\nStarted {effective_count} workers (stagger: {stagger_secs}s between launches).\"\n648\t        );\n649\t        println!(\"Attach to a worker with: tmux attach -t needle-{sanitized_agent}-<name>\");\n650\t    } else {\n651\t        let worker_id = &worker_ids[0];\n652\t        println!(\"Attach with: tmux attach -t needle-{sanitized_agent}-{worker_id}\");\n653\t    }\n654\t\n655\t    Ok(())\n656\t}\n657\t\n658\t/// Initialize the tracing subscriber with OTLP layer if configured.\n659\t///\n660\t/// This must be called before any tracing spans are created so that the OTLP\n661\t/// layer can export them to the configured collector.\n662\t///\n663\t/// Note: Shutdown is handled by the OtlpSink in the telemetry module, not here.\n664\t#[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n665\tfn init_tracing_subscriber(\n666\t    worker_id: String,\n667\t    session_id: String,\n668\t    config: &crate::config::Config,\n669\t) -> Result<()> {\n670\t    use opentelemetry::trace::TracerProvider;\n671\t    use tracing_subscriber::{layer::SubscriberExt, util::SubscriberInitExt};\n672\t\n673\t    let use_ansi = use_ansi();\n674\t\n675\t    // Check if OTLP is enabled\n676\t    if !config.telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled {\n677\t        // No OTLP - just initialize with fmt layer\n678\t        let fmt_layer = tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer()\n679\t            .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n680\t            .with_ansi(use_ansi);\n681\t        tracing_subscriber::registry()\n682\t            .with(fmt_layer)\n683\t            .try_init()\n684\t            .context(\"failed to initialize tracing subscriber\")?;\n685\t        return Ok(());\n686\t    }\n687\t\n688\t    // OTLP is enabled - create the OTLP layer inline\n689\t    // We create it inline to avoid type erasure issues with boxed layers\n690\t    let otlp_config = &config.telemetry.otlp_sink;\n691\t\n692\t    // Build resource attributes\n693\t    let resource = crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_resource(\n694\t        &worker_id,\n695\t        &session_id,\n696\t        otlp_config,\n697\t        Some(&config.agent.default),\n698\t        None, // model - not available in AgentConfig\n699\t        config.workspace.default.to_str(),\n700\t    )\n701\t    .context(\"failed to build OTel resource\")?;\n702\t\n703\t    // Create drop channel for tracing layer\n704\t    let (drop_tx, mut drop_rx) =\n705\t        tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel::<crate::telemetry::otlp::DropEvent>();\n706\t    tokio::spawn(async move {\n707\t        while let Some(drop) = drop_rx.recv().await {\n708\t            tracing::warn!(\n709\t                signal = drop.signal.as_str(),\n710\t                dropped_count = drop.dropped_count,\n711\t                \"OTLP tracing layer export failure\"\n712\t            );\n713\t        }\n714\t    });\n715\t\n716\t    // Build exporters and tracer provider based on protocol\n717\t    let (tracer_provider, ..) = match otlp_config.protocol.as_str() {\n718\t        \"grpc\" => {\n719\t            crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_grpc_providers(otlp_config, &resource, drop_tx)?\n720\t        }\n721\t        \"http\" | \"http/protobuf\" => {\n722\t            crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_http_providers(otlp_config, &resource, drop_tx)?\n723\t        }\n724\t        other => anyhow::bail!(\"invalid OTLP protocol: {other}, must be 'grpc' or 'http'\"),\n725\t    };\n726\t\n727\t    // Create the OpenTelemetry tracing layer\n728\t    let otlp_layer = tracing_opentelemetry::layer().with_tracer(tracer_provider.tracer(\"needle\"));\n729\t\n730\t    // Create a fmt layer that works with any subscriber implementing LookupSpan\n731\t    // We build this after the OTLP layer to ensure proper type compatibility\n732\t    let subscriber = tracing_subscriber::registry().with(otlp_layer).with(\n733\t        tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer()\n734\t            .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n735\t            .with_ansi(use_ansi),\n736\t    );\n737\t\n738\t    subscriber\n739\t        .try_init()\n740\t        .context(\"failed to initialize tracing The only exception is a re-entrant inner\n/// invocation launched by `launch_in_tmux()`, which is identified by the\n/// `NEEDLE_INNER=1` environment variable and runs the worker directly.\nfn cmd_run(\n    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n    agent: Option<String>,\n    count: u32,\n    identifier: Option<String>,\n    timeout: Option<u64>,\n    resume: bool,\n    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    // Determine workspace root (CLI arg → canonicalized, else global default).\n    let workspace_root = if let Some(ref ws) = workspace {\n        ws.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| ws.clone())\n    } else {\n        let global = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n        global.workspace.default.clone()\n    };\n\n    // Load full resolved config (global → workspace .needle.yaml → env → CLI).\n    let cli_overrides = CliOverrides {\n        workspace: Some(workspace_root.clone()),\n        agent_binary: agent.clone(),\n        max_workers: None,\n        ..Default::default()\n    };\n    let (mut config, _) = ConfigLoader::load_resolved(&workspace_root, cli_overrides)?;\n\n    if let Some(t) = timeout {\n        config.agent.timeout = t;\n    }\n\n    if let Some(hr) = hot_reload {\n        config.self_modification.hot_reload = hr;\n    }\n\n    if resume {\n        // Hot-reload resume: inherit worker identity from --identifier,\n        // load state from heartbeat file + registry, continue from SELECTING.\n        let worker_id = identifier\n            .clone()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string());\n\n        // Load resume state from heartbeat and registry.\n        let resume_state = crate::upgrade::ResumeState::load(&config, &worker_id)?;\n\n        // Emit upgrade.completed telemetry.\n        let current_hash = crate::upgrade::file_hash(\n            &std::env::current_exe().context(\"failed to locate own binary\")?,\n        )\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"unknown\".to_string());\n\n        match &resume_state {\n            Some(state) => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    worker = %worker_id,\n                    binary_hash = %&current_hash[..current_hash.len().min(12)],\n                    beads_processed = state.beads_processed,\n                    session = %state.session,\n                    \"resuming worker after hot-reload\"\n                );\n            }\n            None => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    worker = %worker_id,\n                    binary_hash = %&current_hash[..current_hash.len().min(12)],\n                    \"resuming worker after hot-reload (no prior state found)\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        let tel = crate::telemetry::Telemetry::from_config(worker_id.clone(), &config.telemetry)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"hook telemetry init failed, falling back\");\n                crate::telemetry::Telemetry::new(worker_id.clone())\n            });\n        tel.emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::UpgradeCompleted {\n            new_hash: current_hash,\n        })?;\n\n        return run_worker(config, worker_id);\n    }\n\n    if is_needle_inner() {\n        // Re-entrant inner invocation launched by launch_in_tmux() — run\n        // the worker directly inside the dedicated session already created.\n        let worker_id = identifier\n            .clone()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string());\n        let agent_name = agent.as_deref().unwrap_or(&config.agent.default);\n        let session_name = sanitize_session_name(&format!(\"needle-{agent_name}-{worker_id}\"));\n        tracing::info!(worker = %worker_id, session = %session_name, \"starting worker (inner re-entrant invocation)\");\n        run_worker(config, worker_id)\n    } else {\n        // Always create dedicated tmux sessions, even if already inside tmux.\n        launch_workers(\n            config, workspace, agent, count, identifier, timeout, hot_reload,\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n/// Launch `count` workers in separate tmux sessions with staggered startup delays.\nfn launch_workers(\n    config: Config,\n    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n    agent: Option<String>,\n    count: u32,\n    identifier: Option<String>,\n    timeout: Option<u64>,\n    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let agent_name = agent\n        .as_deref()\n        .unwrap_or(&config.agent.default)\n        .to_string();\n    let stagger_secs = config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds;\n    let max_workers = config.worker.max_workers;\n\n    if count == 0 {\n        bail!(\"--count must be at least 1\");\n    }\n    if count as usize > NATO_ALPHABET.len() {\n        bail!(\n            \"--count {} exceeds the maximum of {} (NATO alphabet size)\",\n            count,\n            NATO_ALPHABET.len()\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Enforce max_workers cap (0 means unlimited).\n    let effective_count = if max_workers > 0 && count > max_workers {\n        tracing::warn!(\n            requested = count,\n            capped_to = max_workers,\n            \"count exceeds max_workers; capping\"\n        );\n        eprintln!(\n            \"Warning: --count {count} exceeds max_workers={max_workers}; launching {max_workers} workers\"\n        );\n        max_workers\n    } else {\n        count\n    };\n\n    // --identifier is only meaningful for a single worker.\n    if effective_count > 1 && identifier.is_some() {\n        bail!(\"--identifier cannot be combined with --count > 1; identifiers are auto-assigned from the NATO alphabet\");\n    }\n\n    // Detect existing sessions to avoid name collisions.\n    let occupied = occupied_worker_ids(&agent_name)?;\n    if !occupied.is_empty() {\n        tracing::info!(\n            occupied = ?occupied,\n            \"found existing worker sessions\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Reject --identifier collision early.\n    if let Some(ref id) = identifier {\n        if occupied.contains(id) {\n            bail!(\n                \"worker '{}' is already running in session 'needle-{}-{}'\",\n                id,\n                agent_name,\n                id\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Build the list of worker IDs, skipping occupied names.\n    let worker_ids: Vec<String> = if effective_count == 1 {\n        vec![identifier.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {\n            // Pick the first available NATO name.\n            NATO_ALPHABET\n                .iter()\n                .find(|name| !occupied.contains(**name))\n                .map(|s| s.to_string())\n                .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string())\n        })]\n    } else {\n        let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(effective_count as usize);\n        for name in NATO_ALPHABET {\n            if ids.len() >= effective_count as usize {\n                break;\n            }\n            if occupied.contains(*name) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    worker_id = %name,\n                    \"skipping occupied worker name\"\n                );\n                continue;\n            }\n            ids.push(name.to_string());\n        }\n        if ids.len() < effective_count as usize {\n            bail!(\n                \"cannot launch {} workers — only {} NATO names available ({} occupied)\",\n                effective_count,\n                ids.len(),\n                occupied.len()\n            );\n        }\n        ids\n    };\n\n    for (seq, worker_id) in worker_ids.iter().enumerate() {\n        let session_name = sanitize_session_name(&format!(\"needle-{agent_name}-{worker_id}\"));\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            worker_id = %worker_id,\n            sequence = seq,\n            total = effective_count,\n            session = %session_name,\n            \"launching worker\"\n        );\n\n        // Stagger: sleep before launching subsequent workers.\n        if seq > 0 && stagger_secs > 0 {\n            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(stagger_secs));\n        }\n\n        launch_in_tmux(\n            &session_name,\n            workspace.clone(),\n            agent.clone(),\n            Some(worker_id.clone()),\n            timeout,\n            hot_reload,\n        )?;\n\n        println!(\n            \"[{}/{}] Started worker '{}' in tmux session: {session_name}\",\n            seq + 1,\n            effective_count,\n            worker_id\n        );\n    }\n\n    let sanitized_agent = sanitize_session_name(&agent_name);\n    if effective_count > 1 {\n        println!(\n            \"\\nStarted {effective_count} workers (stagger: {stagger_secs}s between launches).\"\n        );\n        println!(\"Attach to a worker with: tmux attach -t needle-{sanitized_agent}-<name>\");\n    } else {\n        let worker_id = &worker_ids[0];\n        println!(\"Attach with: tmux attach -t needle-{sanitized_agent}-{worker_id}\");\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Initialize the tracing subscriber with OTLP layer if configured.\n///\n/// This must be called before any tracing spans are created so that the OTLP\n/// layer can export them to the configured collector.\n///\n/// Note: Shutdown is handled by the OtlpSink in the telemetry module, not here.\n#[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\nfn init_tracing_subscriber(\n    worker_id: String,\n    session_id: String,\n    config: &crate::config::Config,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    use opentelemetry::trace::TracerProvider;\n    use tracing_subscriber::{layer::SubscriberExt, util::SubscriberInitExt};\n\n    let use_ansi = use_ansi();\n\n    // Check if OTLP is enabled\n    if !config.telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled {\n        // No OTLP - just initialize with fmt layer\n        let fmt_layer = tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer()\n            .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n            .with_ansi(use_ansi);\n        tracing_subscriber::registry()\n            .with(fmt_layer)\n            .try_init()\n            .context(\"failed to initialize tracing subscriber\")?;\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    // OTLP is enabled - create the OTLP layer inline\n    // We create it inline to avoid type erasure issues with boxed layers\n    let otlp_config = &config.telemetry.otlp_sink;\n\n    // Build resource attributes\n    let resource = crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_resource(\n        &worker_id,\n        &session_id,\n        otlp_config,\n        Some(&config.agent.default),\n        None, // model - not available in AgentConfig\n        config.workspace.default.to_str(),\n    )\n    .context(\"failed to build OTel resource\")?;\n\n    // Create drop channel for tracing layer\n    let (drop_tx, mut drop_rx) =\n        tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel::<crate::telemetry::otlp::DropEvent>();\n    tokio::spawn(async move {\n        while let Some(drop) = drop_rx.recv().await {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                signal = drop.signal.as_str(),\n                dropped_count = drop.dropped_count,\n                \"OTLP tracing layer export failure\"\n            );\n        }\n    });\n\n    // Build exporters and tracer provider based on protocol\n    let (tracer_provider, ..) = match otlp_config.protocol.as_str() {\n        \"grpc\" => {\n            crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_grpc_providers(otlp_config, &resource, drop_tx)?\n        }\n        \"http\" | \"http/protobuf\" => {\n            crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_http_providers(otlp_config, &resource, drop_tx)?\n        }\n        other => anyhow::bail!(\"invalid OTLP protocol: {other}, must be 'grpc' or 'http'\"),\n    };\n\n    // Create the OpenTelemetry tracing layer\n    let otlp_layer = tracing_opentelemetry::layer().with_tracer(tracer_provider.tracer(\"needle\"));\n\n    // Create a fmt layer that works with any subscriber implementing LookupSpan\n    // We build this after the OTLP layer to ensure proper type compatibility\n    let subscriber = tracing_subscriber::registry().with(otlp_layer).with(\n        tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer()\n            .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n            .with_ansi(use_ansi),\n    );\n\n    subscriber\n        .try_init()\n        .context(\"failed to initialize tracing subscriber with OTLP\")?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// No-op tracing initialization when OTLP feature is disabled.\n#[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\nfn init_tracing_subscriber(\n    _worker_id: String,\n    _session_id: String,\n    _config: &crate::config::Config,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    use tracing_subscriber::{layer::SubscriberExt, util::SubscriberInitExt};\n\n    let use_ansi = use_ansi();\n\n    // Initialize with just the stdout layer when OTLP is disabled\n    tracing_subscriber::registry()\n        .with(\n            tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer()\n                .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n                .with_ansi(use_ansi),\n        )\n        .try_init()\n        .context(\"failed to initialize tracing subscriber\")?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Helper function to determine ANSI support (non-Android platforms).\n#[cfg(not(target_os = \"android\"))]\nfn use_ansi() -> bool {\n    atty::is(atty::Stream::Stderr)\n}\n\n/// Helper function for Android (no ANSI).\n#[cfg(target_os = \"android\")]\nfn use_ansi() -> bool {\n    false\n}\n\n/// Generate a session ID for a worker.\n///\n/// Uses the telemetry module's session ID generator.\nfn generate_session_id_for_worker() -> String {\n    crate::telemetry::generate_session_id()\n}\n\n/// Start the worker state machine (called when inside tmux or for direct mode).\n///\n/// Creates telemetry and the tokio runtime *before* any other initialization\n/// so that `worker.booting` is the very first JSONL event. Each subsequent\n/// init step is wrapped with `init.step.started` / `init.step.completed` so a\n/// silent hang pinpoints the exact blocking call.\nfn run_worker(config: Config, worker_name: String) -> Result<()> {\n    let boot_start = Instant::now();\n    let qualified_id = format!(\"{}-{}\", config.agent.default, worker_name);\n\n    // Phase 0: create tokio runtime + telemetry, emit worker.booting immediately.\n    // Emit eprintln diagnostics before each step so hangs are visible even if telemetry fails.\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: creating tokio runtime...\");\n    let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().context(\"failed to create tokio runtime\")?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: tokio runtime created\");\n\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: initializing tracing subscriber...\");\n    let session_id = generate_session_id_for_worker();\n    init_tracing_subscriber(qualified_id.clone(), session_id.clone(), &config)?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: tracing subscriber initialized\");\n\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: creating telemetry...\");\n    let telemetry =\n        Telemetry::from_config(qualified_id.clone(), &config.telemetry).unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to create hook-enabled telemetry, falling back\");\n            Telemetry::new(qualified_id.clone())\n        });\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: telemetry created\");\n\n    // Emit worker.booting SYNCHRONOUSLY before starting the async writer.\n    // This guarantees the event is written to disk even if start_and_wait() hangs.\n    // Fixes the silent pre-init deadlock where the JSONL file is created but empty.\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: emitting worker.booting event (sync)...\");\n    telemetry.emit_sync(EventKind::WorkerBooting {\n        worker_name: worker_name.clone(),\n        version: env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\").to_string(),\n    })?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: worker.booting written to disk\");\n\n    // Start the async writer thread after worker.booting is on disk.\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: starting telemetry writer thread...\");\n    rt.block_on(telemetry.start_and_wait())\n        .context(\"writer thread failed to start\")?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: writer thread started\");\n\n    // Phase 1: bead store discovery.\n    // Use BfCliBeadStore for atomic server-selected bead claiming.\n    let store: Arc<dyn crate::bead_store::BeadStore> =\n        Arc::new(init_step(\"bead_store_discover\", &telemetry, || {\n            crate::bead_store::BfCliBeadStore::discover(\n                config.workspace.default.clone(),\n                None,                       // model: do not filter by model — beads are untagged\n                Some(\"needle\".to_string()), // harness\n                Some(env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\").to_string()), // harness_version\n            )\n            .context(\"failed to locate bf CLI for bead store\")\n        })?);\n\n    // Phase 2: worker construction (heavy — prompt loading, adapter discovery, etc.).\n    let mut worker = init_step(\"worker_construction\", &telemetry, || {\n        Ok(Worker::new_with_telemetry(\n            config,\n            worker_name.clone(),\n            store,\n            telemetry.clone(),\n        ))\n    })?;\n\n    // Boot timeout guard: self-abort if init took >60 s.\n    let elapsed_ms = boot_start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;\n    if elapsed_ms > 60_000 {\n        telemetry.emit(EventKind::WorkerBootTimeout { elapsed_ms })?;\n        bail!(\"boot exceeded 60 s ({elapsed_ms} ms), aborting\");\n    }\n\n    eprintln!(\n        \"NEEDLE worker boot: all init steps completed in {elapsed_ms}ms, starting worker loop...\"\n    );\n    let result = rt.block_on(worker.run())?;\n\n    tracing::info!(final_state = %result, \"worker finished\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Emit start/complete telemetry around a fallible initialization step.\n///\n/// Each step's completion is force-flushed to disk so that if a subsequent\n/// step blocks indefinitely, the telemetry log shows exactly where it stopped.\n/// Also emits eprintln diagnostics for visibility even if telemetry hangs.\nfn init_step<T, F>(name: &str, tel: &Telemetry, f: F) -> Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: FnOnce() -> Result<T>,\n{\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: starting init step '{name}'...\");\n    tel.emit(EventKind::InitStepStarted {\n        step: name.to_string(),\n    })?;\n    let t = Instant::now();\n    let result = f();\n    let elapsed = t.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;\n    tel.emit(EventKind::InitStepCompleted {\n        step: name.to_string(),\n        duration_ms: elapsed,\n    })?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: init step '{name}' completed in {elapsed}ms\");\n    // Force-flush so the step completion is visible before the next (potentially blocking) step.\n    tel.force_flush(std::time::Duration::from_secs(1))?;\n    result\n}\n\n/// Returns true when this process is a re-entrant inner invocation launched\n/// by `launch_in_tmux()`, indicated by `NEEDLE_INNER=1` in the environment.\nfn is_needle_inner() -> bool {\n    std::env::var(\"NEEDLE_INNER\").is_ok_and(|v| v == \"1\")\n}\n\n/// Create a single tmux session and re-exec self inside it with `--count 1`.\nfn launch_in_tmux(\n    session_name: &str,\n    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n    agent: Option<String>,\n    identifier: Option<String>,\n    timeout: Option<u64>,\n    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    // Build the command that tmux will run inside the session.\n    let self_exe = std::env::current_exe().context(\"failed to locate own binary\")?;\n    let mut inner_args = vec![\"run\".to_string()];\n\n    if let Some(ref ws) = workspace {\n        inner_args.push(\"--workspace\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(ws.display().to_string());\n    }\n    if let Some(ref a) = agent {\n        inner_args.push(\"--agent\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(a.clone());\n    }\n    // Each session runs exactly one worker; identifier is always resolved before call.\n    inner_args.push(\"--count\".to_string());\n    inner_args.push(\"1\".to_string());\n    if let Some(ref id) = identifier {\n        inner_args.push(\"--identifier\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(id.clone());\n    }\n    if let Some(t) = timeout {\n        inner_args.push(\"--timeout\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(t.to_string());\n    }\n    if let Some(hr) = hot_reload {\n        inner_args.push(\"--hot-reload\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(hr.to_string());\n    }\n\n    // Build stderr log path: ~/.needle/logs/<session_name>.stderr.log\n    let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \".\".to_string());\n    let stderr_log = format!(\"{home}/.needle/logs/{session_name}.stderr.log\");\n\n    let inner_cmd = format!(\n        \"NEEDLE_INNER=1 {} {} 2>> {}\",\n        shell_escape(&self_exe.display().to_string()),\n        inner_args\n            .iter()\n            .map(|a| shell_escape(a))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(\" \"),\n        shell_escape(&stderr_log)\n    );\n\n    let status = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n        .args([\"new-session\", \"-d\", \"-s\", session_name, &inner_cmd])\n        .status()\n        .context(\"failed to launch tmux — is tmux installed?\")?;\n\n    if !status.success() {\n        bail!(\n            \"tmux new-session exited with status {} for session '{}'\",\n            status,\n            session_name\n        );\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// `needle stop` — send SIGTERM to worker processes in tmux sessions.\nfn cmd_stop(all: bool, identifier: Option<String>) -> Result<()> {\n    if !all && identifier.is_none() {\n        bail!(\"specify --all or --identifier <NAME>\");\n    }\n\n    let sessions = list_needle_sessions()?;\n\n    if sessions.is_empty() {\n        println!(\"No needle sessions running.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let targets: Vec<&str> = if all {\n        sessions.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect()\n    } else {\n        let id = identifier.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"\");\n        sessions\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|s| s.name.contains(id))\n            .map(|s| s.name.as_str())\n            .collect()\n    };\n\n    if targets.is_empty() {\n        println!(\"No matching sessions found.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    for session in &targets {\n        tracing::info!(session = %session, \"sending SIGTERM to tmux session\");\n        // tmux send-keys sends C-c to the foreground process\n        let status = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n            .args([\"send-keys\", \"-t\", session, \"C-c\", \"\"])\n            .status()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to send SIGTERM to session '{session}'\"))?;\n\n        if status.success() {\n            // Wait up to 5 seconds for the worker to exit gracefully\n            for _ in 0..50 {\n                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));\n                let session_exists = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n                    .args([\"has-session\", \"-t\", session])\n                    .output()\n                    .map(|o| o.status.success())\n                    .unwrap_or(false);\n                if !session_exists {\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            // Kill the session to clean up (worker may have already exited)\n            let kill_status = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n                .args([\"kill-session\", \"-t\", session])\n                .status();\n            match kill_status {\n                Ok(s) if s.success() => println!(\"Stopped: {session}\"),\n                Ok(_) => println!(\"Stopped: {session} (session already gone)\"),\n                Err(e) => println!(\"Warning: stopped {session} but failed to kill session: {e}\"),\n            }\n        } else {\n            println!(\"Warning: could not stop session '{session}' (status: {status})\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// `needle cleanup` — remove orphaned tmux sessions.\n///\n/// Finds and removes needle tmux sessions that no longer have active workers.\n/// With --all, removes all needle sessions regardless of worker status.\nfn cmd_cleanup(all: bool, identifier: Option<String>) -> Result<()> {\n    let sessions = list_needle_sessions()?;\n\n    if sessions.is_empty() {\n        println!(\"No needle sessions running.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let targets: Vec<&str> = if all {\n        sessions.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect()\n    } else {\n        let id = identifier.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"\");\n        sessions\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|s| id.is_empty() || s.name.contains(id))\n            .map(|s| s.name.as_str())\n            .collect()\n    };\n\n    if targets.is_empty() {\n        println!(\"No matching sessions found.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let mut cleaned = 0;\n    for session in &targets {\n        // Kill the session\n        let status = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n            .args([\"kill-session\", \"-t\", session])\n            .status();\n\n        match status {\n            Ok(s) if s.success() => {\n                println!(\"Cleaned up: {session}\");\n                cleaned += 1;\n            }\n            Ok(_) => {\n                println!(\"Warning: session '{session}' already gone\");\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                println!(\"Warning: failed to cleanup session '{session}': {e}\");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if cleaned == 0 {\n        println!(\"No sessions cleaned up.\");\n    } else {\n        println!(\"Cleaned up {cleaned} session(s).\");\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// `needle list` — show running needle sessions.\nfn cmd_list(format: ListFormat) -> Result<()> {\n    let sessions = list_needle_sessions()?;\n\n    if sessions.is_empty() {\n        match format {\n            ListFormat::Table => println!(\"No needle sessions running.\"),\n            ListFormat::Json => println!(\"[]\"),\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    match format {\n        ListFormat::Table => {\n            println!(\"{:<40} {:<20} {:<10}\", \"SESSION\", \"CREATED\", \"STATUS\");\n            println!(\"{}\", \"-\".repeat(70));\n            for s in &sessions {\n                println!(\"{:<40} {:<20} {:<10}\", s.name, s.created, s.status);\n            }\n        }\n        ListFormat::Json => {\n            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&sessions)\n                .context(\"failed to serialize sessions to JSON\")?;\n            println!(\"{json}\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// `needle init` — initialize v2 config with optional v1 migration.\n///\n/// Creates ~/.config/needle/config.yaml. Detects existing v1 artifacts\n/// in ~/.needle/ and migrates compatible settings (agent name, workspace\n/// path, worker count) to the v2 YAML schema. Safe to run on already-\n/// initialized installs (idempotent).\nfn cmd_init() -> Result<()> {\n    /// Resolve a path relative to the user's home directory.\n    fn dirs_or_home(relative: &str) -> PathBuf {\n        if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os(\"HOME\") {\n            PathBuf::from(home).join(relative)\n        } else {\n            PathBuf::from(\"/tmp\").join(relative)\n        }\n    }\n\n    let config_path = dirs_or_home(\".config/needle/config.yaml\");\n    let v1_dir = dirs_or_home(\".needle\");\n\n    // Check if v2 config already exists.\n    if config_path.exists() {\n        println!(\"Config already exists: {}\", config_path.display());\n        let config = ConfigLoader::load_from_path(&config_path)?;\n        println!(\"  Agent default: {}\", config.agent.default);\n        println!(\"  Workspace: {}\", config.workspace.default.display());\n        println!(\"  Max workers: {}\", config.worker.max_workers);\n        println!(\"\\nTo reinitialize, delete the existing config file first.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    // Detect v1 artifacts and migrate compatible settings.\n    let mut agent_name = None::<String>;\n    let mut workspace_path = None::<PathBuf>;\n\n    // Check for v1 directory.\n    if v1_dir.exists() && v1_dir.is_dir() {\n        println!(\"Detected v1 artifacts: {}\", v1_dir.display());\n\n        // Look for v1 config hints (file-based heuristics).\n        // v1 stored agent name as a subdirectory: ~/.needle/<agent>/\n        if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&v1_dir) {\n            for entry in entries.flatten() {\n                let path = entry.path();\n                if path.is_dir() {\n                    let name = path.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str());\n                    // Skip common non-agent subdirectories.\n                    if let Some(name) = name {\n                        if !matches!(name, \"state\" | \"logs\" | \"canary\" | \"config\") {\n                            agent_name = Some(name.to_string());\n                            println!(\"  Migrating agent name from v1: {}\", name);\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // v1 workspace hints: look for recent .beads directories under $HOME.\n        let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \".\".to_string());\n        let home_path = PathBuf::from(&home);\n        if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&home_path) {\n            for entry in entries.flatten() {\n                let path = entry.path();\n                if path.is_dir() && path.join(\".beads\").exists() {\n                    // Prefer the most recently modified workspace.\n                    let modified = entry\n                        .metadata()\n                        .and_then(|m| m.modified())\n                        .unwrap_or(std::time::SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH);\n                    let current_best = workspace_path\n                        .as_ref()\n                        .and_then(|p| std::fs::metadata(p).ok()?.modified().ok())\n                        .unwrap_or(std::time::SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH);\n                    if modified > current_best {\n                        workspace_path = Some(path.clone());\n                        println!(\"  Migrating workspace path from v1: {}\", path.display());\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Build the config with migrated values or defaults.\n    let default_config = Config::default();\n    let agent_default = agent_name.unwrap_or_else(|| default_config.agent.default.clone());\n    let workspace_default =\n        workspace_path.unwrap_or_else(|| default_config.workspace.default.clone());\n\n    // Construct a minimal config YAML with comments explaining each field.\n    let config_yaml = format!(\n        r#\"# NEEDLE v2 Configuration\n# Migrated from v1: {v1_status}\n#\n# This file controls NEEDLE's global behavior. Workspace-specific overrides\n# can be placed in .needle.yaml within each workspace directory.\n#\n# Resolution order (later overrides earlier):\n#   1. Built-in defaults\n#   2. ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// `needle attach <identifier>` — attach to a running worker's tmux session.\nfn cmd_attach(identifier: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    let sessions = list_needle_sessions()?;\n\n    if sessions.is_empty() {\n        bail!(\"no needle sessions running\");\n    }\n\n    // Find matching session: exact match on identifier portion or substring match on full name.\n    let matches: Vec<&TmuxSession> = sessions\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|s| s.name.ends_with(&format!(\"-{identifier}\")) || s.name.contains(identifier))\n        .collect();\n\n    if matches.is_empty() {\n        let available: Vec<&str> = sessions.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect();\n        bail!(\n            \"no session matching '{}'; available: {}\",\n            identifier,\n            available.join(\", \")\n        );\n    }\n\n    if matches.len() > 1 {\n        let names: Vec<&str> = matches.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect();\n        bail!(\n            \"ambiguous identifier '{}'; matches: {}\",\n            identifier,\n            names.join(\", \")\n        );\n    }\n\n    let session = &matches[0].name;\n    let status = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n        .args([\"attach-session\", \"-t\", session])\n        .status()\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to attach to tmux session '{session}'\"))?;\n\n    if !status.success() {\n        bail!(\"tmux attach-session exited with status {status} for '{session}'\");\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// `needle status` — show fleet status summary.\nfn cmd_status(\n    format: ListFormat,\n    by_worker: bool,\n    cost: bool,\n    since: Option<String>,\n    until: Option<String>,\n stats` — show outcome statistics from telemetry logs.\nfn cmd_stats(\n    by: StatsBy,\n    since: Option<String>,\n    until: Option<String>,\n    format: ListFormat,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    use crate::stats::{compute_stats, StatsDimension};\n\n    let config = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n    let log_dir = config.workspace.home.join(\"logs\");\n\n    let since_dt = since.as_deref().map(telemetry::parse_since).transpose()?;\n    let until_dt = until.as_deref().map(telemetry::parse_until).transpose()?;\n    let events = telemetry::read_logs(&log_dir, since_dt, until_dt, None)?;\n\n    let dimension = match by {\n        StatsBy::TemplateVersion => StatsDimension::TemplateVersion,\n        StatsBy::TaskType => StatsDimension::TaskType,\n        StatsBy::Worker => StatsDimension::Worker,\n    };\n\n    let mut rows = compute_stats(&events, dimension);\n    // Sort by beads descending so most active groups appear first.\n    rows.sort_by(|a, b| b.beads.cmp(&a.beads).then(a.key.cmp(&b.key)));\n\n    let dim_label = match by {\n        StatsBy::TemplateVersion => \"TEMPLATE VERSION\",\n        StatsBy::TaskType => \"TASK TYPE\",\n        StatsBy::Worker => \"WORKER\",\n    };\n\n    match format {\n        ListFormat::Table => {\n            if rows.is_empty() {\n                println!(\"No telemetry data found.\");\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n            let key_width = rows.iter().map(|r| r.key.len()).max().unwrap_or(16).max(16);\n            println!(\n                \"{:<width$} {:>6} {:>6} {:>6} {:>8} {:>9} {:>10} {:>12}\",\n                dim_label,\n                \"BEADS\",\n                \"PASS\",\n                \"FAIL\",\n                \"TIMEOUT\",\n                \"PASS RATE\",\n                \"AVG TOK\",\n                \"AVG COST\",\n                width = key_width,\n            );\n            println!(\n                \"{}\",\n                \"-\".repeat(key_width + 6 + 6 + 6 + 8 + 9 + 10 + 12 + 7)\n            );\n            for row in &rows {\n                let pass_rate = row\n                    .pass_rate()\n                    .map(|r| format!(\"{:.1}%\", r * 100.0))\n                    .unwrap_or_else(|| \"-\".to_string());\n                let avg_tok = row\n                    .avg_tokens()\n                    .map(|t| format!(\"{:.0}\", t))\n                    .unwrap_or_else(|| \"-\".to_string());\n                let avg_cost = row\n                    .avg_cost_usd()\n                    .map(|c| format!(\"${:.5}\", c))\n                    .unwrap_or_else(|| \"-\".to_string());\n                println!(\n                    \"{:<width$} {:>6} {:>6} {:>6} {:>8} {:>9} {:>10} {:>12}\",\n                    row.key,\n                    row.beads,\n                    row.pass,\n                    row.fail,\n                    row.timeout,\n                    pass_rate,\n                    avg_tok,\n Every design decision in this plan traces back to one or more of them.\n8\t\n9\t1. **Deterministic order.** Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same bead ordering. There is no randomness in selection. Ties are broken by creation time.\n10\t\n11\t2. **Explicit outcome paths.** Every possible result of every operation has a named handler. If an outcome can happen, it has a handler. If it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen. The type system enforces exhaustiveness.\n12\t\n13\t3. **Platform and model agnostic.** NEEDLE wraps any headless CLI that accepts a prompt and exits. It runs on any POSIX system. It does not depend on any specific AI provider, model, or API.\n14\t\n15\t4. **Observable by default.** Every state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome emits structured telemetry. A silent worker is a broken worker. Telemetry is structured from origin (JSONL) and exportable as OpenTelemetry (OTLP) so any compliant backend — Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, FABRIC — can consume NEEDLE's signals without a custom adapter.\n16\t\n17\t5. **Self-healing.** Workers detect and recover from stuck states, stale claims, crashed peers, and corrupted databases without human intervention. Recovery paths are explicit, not heuristic.\n18\t\n19\t6. **Separation of concerns.** The orchestrator does not execute work. The agent does not manage state. The bead store does not enforce workflow. Each component has one job.\n20\t\n21\t---\n22\t\n23\t## Architecture Overview\n24\t\n25\tNEEDLE is composed of five layers:\n26\t\n27\t```\n28\t┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n29\t│                        CLI Layer                              │\n30\t│  needle run | stop | list | attach | status | config          │\n31\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n32\t│                     Worker Layer                              │\n33\t│  Worker loop, strand waterfall, session management            │\n34\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n35\t│                  Coordination Layer                            │\n36\t│  Claiming, locking, heartbeats, peer awareness                │\n37\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n38\t│                    Agent Layer                                 │\n39\t│  Adapter interface, dispatch, result capture                  │\n40\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n41\t│                   Foundation Layer                             │\n42\t│  Telemetry, configuration, bead store interface, self-healing │\n43\t└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n44\t```\n45\t\n46\t### Component Map\n47\t\n48\t| Component | Responsibility | Inputs | Outputs |\n49\t|-----------|---------------|--------|---------|\n50\t| **CLI** | Parse commands, manage sessions | User commands | Worker processes |\n51\t| **Worker** | Execute the strand waterfall loop | Bead queue state | Dispatch requests, state transitions |\n52\t| **StrandRunner** | Evaluate strands in sequence | Queue state, |\n70\t|-------------|-----|--------|\n71\t| Exhaustive pattern matching | Every outcome must be handled; compiler enforces it | Principle 2, bead-lifecycle-bugs.md |\n72\t| Real module system | 45K single-file bash was unmaintainable | bash-at-scale-problems.md |\n73\t| Structured error types | Silent failures caused cascading bugs | claim-race-conditions.md |\n74\t| Native JSON support | Fragile jq parsing corrupted state | worker-starvation-lessons.md |\n75\t| Proper concurrency primitives | flock/trap/PID files were inadequate | concurrency-approaches-compared.md |\n76\t| Single binary distribution | NEEDLE must be trivially installable | Principle 3 |\n77\t| Cross-platform | Linux, macOS at minimum | Principle 3 |\n78\t| Static analysis | Catch undefined functions, unused variables at compile time | bundler-build-integrity.md |\n79\t\n80\t**Recommended: Rust.** Exhaustive `match`, `Result<T, E>` error handling, `serde_json`, `tokio` for async, single binary via static linking, cross-compilation. The beads ecosystem already has Rust precedent (beads_rust, beads-polis).\n81\t\n82\t**Acceptable alternative: Go.** Simpler learning curve, good concurrency, single binary. Lacks exhaustive matching (requires discipline instead of compiler enforcement).\n83\t\n84\t**Not acceptable: Bash, Python, Node.** Bash failed at scale (documented). Python/Node require runtime dependencies, violating single-binary distribution.\n85\t\n86\t---\n87\t\n88\t## Key Decisions from Research\n89\t\n90\tThese decisions are informed by the 14 research files in `docs/research/`:\n91\t\n92\t| Decision | Chosen Approach | Alternative Considered | Why |\n93\t|----------|----------------|----------------------|-----|\n94\t| Bead store interface | Abstract trait over `br` CLI | Direct SQLite access | Platform agnostic; works with future bead backends |\n95\t| Claim atomicity | `br update --claim` + workspace flock | Central coordinator (Perles) | No SPOF; works with decentralized workers |\n96\t| Heartbeat model | File-based heartbeat with TTL (from beads-polis) | Shared memory | Survives worker crashes; observable by peers |\n97\t| Validation gates | Pluggable gate system (inspired by bg-gate) | Hardcoded checks | Different workspaces need different validation |\n98\t| Work decomposition | Built-in mitosis with child-aware dedup | External only (spec2beads) | Mitosis is valid when the split criteria are semantic (multi-task detection) and dedup checks the parent's existing children |\n99\t| Self-modification | Allowed with release channel promotion (testing → stable → fleet hot-reload) | Prohibited entirely | v1 failures came from untested changes deploying directly to the fleet. Canary testing with defined inputs/outputs prevents this. |\n100\t| Workspace discovery | Explicit configuration | Filesystem scanning | Explore strand's unbounded find caused 35+ load |\n101\t| Alert system | Verify-then-alert with rate limiting | Alert-on-empty | 100% false positive rate from naive alerting |\n102\t\n103\t## Key Decisions from Operational Learnings\n104\t\n105\tThese decisions are informed by the 9 notes files in `docs/notes/`:\n106\t\n107\t| Learning | Design Response |\n108\t|----------|----------------|\n109\t| Mitosis explosion (5,741 duplicate beads) | Mitosis checks parent's existing children before creating new ones. Duplicate splits are structurally impossible. Split criteria are semantic (multi-task detection), not numeric. |\n110\t| 100% false positive starvation alerts | Three-state model: no beads exist / all claimed / invisible. Verify independently before alerting. |\n111\t| Bundler shipped undefined functions | Compiled language eliminates this class entirely. |\n112\t| Agent-owned closure most reliable | NEEDLE does not close beads. Agent receives `br close <id>` instruction in prompt. |\n113\t| stdout/stderr corruption | Telemetry is a structured system, never interleaved with agent output. |\n114\t| Workers modifying their own orchestrator | Self-modification allowed via release channels. New builds must pass canary tests in isolation before promotion to `:stable`. Fleet hot-reloads from `:stable`, never from `:testing`. |\n115\t| ~20 worker practical limit (EX44) | Fleet sizing is bounded by three runtime factors: provider inference throughput, available CPU, and available RAM. NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated. Staggered launch is default. |\n116\t| Bead granularity affects success rate | Document guidelines but don't enforce — this is a bead authoring concern, not orchestration. |\n117\t\n118\t---\n119\t\n120\t# State Machine\n121\t\n122\tThe worker loop is a finite state machine. Every state has defined entry conditions, actions, and exit transitions. There are no implicit states or fallthrough paths.\n123\t\n124\t## Worker States\n125\t\n126\t```\n127\t                    ┌──────────┐\n128\t                    │  BOOTING │\n129\t                    └────┬─────┘\n130\t                         │ config loaded, health check passed\n131\t                         ▼\n132\t                    ┌──────────┐\n133\t              ┌────►│ SELECTING│◄──────────────────────────────┐\n134\t              │     └────┬─────┘                                │\n135\t              │          │ candidate found                      │\n136\t              │          ▼                                      │\n137\t              │     ┌──────────┐  race lost (retry < max)      │\n138\t              │     │ CLAIMING │──────────────────────────┐    │\n139\t              │     └────┬─────┘                           │    │\n140\t              │          │ claimed                         │    │\n141\t              │          ▼                                 ▼    │\n142\t              │     ┌──────────┐                     ┌────────┐│\n143\t              │     │ BUILDING │                     │RETRYING││\n144\t              │     └────┬─────┘                     └────┬───┘│\n145\t              │          │ prompt ready                   │     │\n146\t              │          ▼                                └─────┘\n147\t              │     ┌────────────┐\n148\t              │     │DISPATCHING │\n149\t              │     └────┬───────┘\n150\t              │          │ agent process started\n151\t              │          ▼\n152\t              │     ┌──────────┐\n153\t              │     │ EXECUTING│\n154\t              │     └────┬─────┘\n155\t              │          │ agent exited\n156\t              │          ▼\n157\t              │     ┌──────────┐\n158\t              │     │ HANDLING │\n159\t              │     └────┬─────┘\n160\t              │          │ outcome processed\n161\t              │          ▼\n162\t              │     ┌──────────┐\n163\t              │     │ LOGGING  │\n164\t              │     └────┬─────┘\n165\t              │          │ telemetry emitted\n166\t              └──────────┘\n167\t```\n168\t\n169\t### Terminal States\n170\t\n171\t```\n172\t    ┌───────────┐       ┌───────────┐       ┌───────────┐\n173\t    │ EXHAUSTED │       │  STOPPED  │       │  ERRORED  │\n174\t    └───────────┘       └───────────┘       └───────────┘\n175\t    all strands empty   graceful shutdown   unrecoverable\n176\t```\n177\t\n178\t## State Definitions\n179\t\n180\t### BOOTING\n181\t\n182\t**Entry:** Worker process started.\n183\t\n184\t**Actions:**\n185\t1. Load configuration (global → workspace → CLI overrides)\n186\t2. Validate bead store connectivity (`br doctor` or equivalent)\n187\t3. Register in worker state registry\n188\t4. Emit `worker.started` telemetry event\n189\t5. Start heartbeat emitter\n190\t\n191\t**Transitions:**\n192\t| Condition | Next State |\n193\t|-----------|-----------|\n194\t| Config loaded, bead store healthy | SELECTING |\n195\t| Config invalid | ERRORED |\n196\t| Bead store unreachable | ERRORED (after retry with backoff) |\n197\t\n198\t### SELECTING\n199\t\n200\t**Entry:** Worker is ready for next bead. This is the strand waterfall entry point.\n201\t\n202\t**Actions:**\n203\t1. Emit heartbeat\n204\t2. Evaluate strands in sequence\n205\t3. First strand that yields a candidate bead wins\n206\t\n207\t**Transitions:**\n208\t| Condition | Next State |\n209\t|-----------|-----------|\n210\t| Candidate bead found | CLAIMING |\n211\t| All strands exhausted | EXHAUSTED |\n212\t| Shutdown signal received | STOPPED |\n213\t\n214\t### CLAIMING\n215\t\n216\t**Entry:** A candidate bead has been selected.\n217\t\n218\t**Actions:**\n219\t1. Acquire workspace claim lock (flock, per-workspace)\n220\t2. Verify bead is still claimable (`br show --json`, check status + assignee)\n221\t3. Attempt atomic claim: `br update <id> --claim --actor <worker-id>`\n222\t4. Release workspace claim lock\n223\t5. Emit `bead.claim.attempted` telemetry\n224\t\n225\t**Transitions:**\n226\t| Condition | Exit Code | Next State |\n227\t|-----------|-----------|-----------|\n228\t| Claim succeeded | 0 | BUILDING |\n229\t| Race lost (already claimed) | 4 | RETRYING |\n230\t| Bead no longer claimable (closed, deferred) | 1 | SELECTING |\n231\t| Bead store error | >0 | SELECTING (after backoff) |\n232\t| Max retries exceeded | — | SELECTING (exclude this bead, reset retry counter) |\n233\t\n234\t### RETRYING\n235\t\n236\t**Entry:** A claim attempt failed due to race condition.\n237\t\n238\t**Actions:**\n239\t1. Increment retry counter for this selection cycle\n240\t2. Add failed bead ID to exclusion set\n241\t3. Emit `bead.claim.race_lost` telemetry\n242\t\n243\t**Transitions:**\n244\t| Condition | Next State |\n245\t|-----------|-----------|\n246\t| Retry count < max_retries (default: 5) | CLAIMING (with next candidate from same strand) |\n247\t| Retry count >= max_retries | SELECTING (reset, move to next strand) |\n248\t\n249\t### BUILDING\n250\t\n251\t**Entry:** Bead is claimed by this worker.\n252\t\n253\t**Actions:**\n254\t1. Read full bead context: title, body, dependencies, labels, workspace path\n255\t2. Read workspace context: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .beads/config.yaml\n256\t3. Construct prompt from template (deterministic: same bead → same prompt)\n257\t4. Include bead ID and `br close <id>` instruction in prompt\n258\t5. Emit `prompt.built` telemetry (bead ID, prompt hash, token estimate)\n259\t\n260\t**Transitions:**\n261\t| Condition | Next State |\n262\t|-----------|-----------|\n263\t| Prompt built successfully | DISPATCHING |\n264\t| Bead context unreadable | HANDLING (outcome: failure, release bead) |\n265\t\n266\t### DISPATCHING\n267\t\n268\t**Entry:** Prompt is ready.\n269\t\n270\t**Actions:**\n271\t1. Load agent adapter configuration (YAML)\n272\t2. Resolve invoke template with prompt, workspace path, environment\n273\t3. Start agent process via rendered command\n274\t4. Record process PID, start time\n275\t5. Emit `agent.dispatched` telemetry (agent name, model, workspace)\n276\t\n277\t**Transitions:**\n278\t| Condition | Next State |\n279\t|-----------|-----------|\n280\t| Agent process started | EXECUTING |\n281\t| Agent binary not found | HANDLING (outcome: failure, release bead) |\n282\t| Adapter config invalid | HANDLING (outcome: failure, release bead) |\n283\t\n284\t### EXECUTING\n285\t\n286\t**Entry:** Agent process is running.\n287\t\n288\t**Actions:**\n289\t1. Wait for agent process to exit\n290\t2. Capture stdout, stderr, exit code\n291\t3. Monitor execution timeout\n292\t4. Continue emitting heartbeats while waiting\n293\t5. Emit `agent.executing` heartbeat telemetry periodically\n294\t\n295\t**Transitions:**\n296\t| Condition | Exit Code | Next State |\n297\t|-----------|-----------|-----------|\n298\t| Agent exited normally | any | HANDLING |\n299\t| Execution timeout exceeded | — | Kill process → HANDLING (outcome: timeout) |\n300\t| Shutdown signal received | — | Kill process → HANDLING (outcome: interrupted) |\n301\t\n302\t### HANDLING\n303\t\n304\t**Entry:** Agent has exited (or was killed). This is where outcome routing happens.\n305\t\n306\t**Actions:**\n307\t1. Classify outcome by exit code\n308\t2. Execute the handler for that outcome class\n309\t3. Emit `bead.outcome` telemetry\n310\t\n311\t**Outcome Table:**\n312\t\n313\t| Outcome | Exit Code | Handler | Bead Action |\n314\t|---------|-----------|---------|-------------|\n315\t| **Success** | 0 | Verify bead was closed by agent. If not, log warning (do not auto-close). | None (agent owns closure) |\n316\t| **Failure** | 1 | Evaluate for mitosis (see Mitosis section). If splittable, split and block parent. If not, release bead (`br update --status open --unassign`). Increment failure count via label. | Split or released |\n317\t| **Timeout** | 124 | Release bead. Add `deferred` label. | Released + deferred |\n318\t| **Crash** | >128 (signal) | Release bead. Create alert bead in workspace. | Released + alert |\n319\t| **Race Lost** | 4 | (Handled at CLAIMING, should not reach here) | N/A |\n320\t| **Interrupted** | — | Release bead. Clean shutdown. | Released |\n321\t| **Agent Not Found** | 127 | Release bead. Emit error. Do not retry (config issue). | Released |\n322\t| **Build Failure** | — | Release bead. Emit error. | Released |\n323\t\n324\t**Agent-owned closure:** NEEDLE does not close beads. The agent is instructed (via prompt) to run `br close <id>` upon successful completion. If the bead is still open after a success exit code, NEEDLE logs a warning but does not intervene. This is a deliberate design choice based on operational experience (see `docs/notes/bead-lifecycle-bugs.md`).\n325\t\n326\t**Transitions:**\n327\t| Condition | Next State |\n328\t|-----------|-----------|\n329\t| Outcome processed | LOGGING |\n330\t\n331\t### LOGGING\n332\t\n333\t**Entry:** Outcome has been handled.\n334\t\n335\t**Actions:**\n336\t1. Record effort: elapsed time, exit code, token count (if extractable), estimated cost\n337\t2. Emit `bead.completed` or `bead.released` telemetry\n338\t3. Update worker state registry (beads processed, current streak)\n339\t4. Reset retry counter and exclusion set\n340\t\n341\t**Transitions:**\n342\t| Condition | Next State |\n343\t|-----------|-----------|\n344\t| Logging complete | SELECTING |\n345\t\n346\t### EXHAUSTED\n347\t\n348\t**Entry:** All strands returned no work.\n349\t\n350\t**Actions:**\n351\t1. Emit `worker.exhausted` telemetry\n352\t2. If `idle_timeout` configured, start countdown\n353\t3. If `idle_action` is `wait`, sleep with exponential backoff (max 60s)\n354\t4. If `idle_action` is `exit`, terminate\n355\t\n356\t**Transitions:**\n357\t| Condition | Next State |\n358\t|-----------|-----------|\n359\t| Backoff expired, retry strands | SELECTING |\n360\t| Idle timeout exceeded | STOPPED |\n361\t| Shutdown signal received | STOPPED |\n362\t\n363\t### STOPPED\n364\t\n365\t**Entry:** Graceful shutdown.\n366\t\n367\t**Actions:**\n368\t1. Release any claimed bead\n369\t2. Deregister from worker state registry\n370\t3. Stop heartbeat emitter\n371\t4. Emit `worker.stopped` telemetry\n372\t5. Exit process\n373\t\n374\t**Transitions:** None (terminal).\n375\t\n376\t### ERRORED\n377\t\n378\t**Entry:** Unrecoverable error.\n379\t\n380\t**Actions:**\n381\t1. Release any claimed bead (best-effort)\n382\t2. Emit `worker.errored` telemetry with error details\n383\t3. Deregister from worker state registry (best-effort)\n384\t4. Exit process with non-zero code\n385\t\n386\t**Transitions:** None (terminal).\n387\t\n388\t## Error Model\n389\t\n390\tErrors are classified into three tiers:\n391\t\n392\t### Tier 1: Transient (retry)\n393\t\n394\tTemporary failures that resolve on their own. The worker retries with backoff.\n395\t\n396\t- Bead store temporarily unreachable\n397\t- Claim race lost\n398\t- Lock contention timeout\n399\t- Agent timeout (may succeed on re-dispatch)\n400\t\n401\t### Tier 2: Bead-scoped (release and continue)\n402\t\n403\tFailures specific to one bead. Release it and move on.\n404\t\n405\t- Agent exited with failure\n406\t- Prompt build failed (bead context unreadable)\n407\t- Agent binary missing\n408\t\n409\t### Tier 3: Worker-scoped (exit)\n410\t\n411\tFailures that affect the worker's ability to function. Exit and let the fleet manager handle it.\n412\t\n413\t- Configuration invalid\n414\t- Bead store persistently unreachable\n415\t- Filesystem full\n416\t- Heartbeat file unwritable\n417\t\n418\t## Invariants\n419\t\n420\tThese must hold at all times. Violation of any invariant is a bug.\n421\t\n422\t1. **A worker holds at most one claimed bead.** There is no pipelining or parallel execution within a single worker.\n423\t\n424\t2. **A claimed bead is always released.** Every path through HANDLING releases the bead unless the agent closed it. There is no path where a bead remains claimed after the worker moves to SELECTING.\n425\t\n426\t3. **Heartbeat is continuous.** From BOOTING to STOPPED/ERRORED, the worker emits heartbeats. A gap in heartbeats means the worker is stuck or dead.\n427\t\n428\t4. **Telemetry is emitted for every state transition.** Silent transitions do not exist.\n429\t\n430\t5. **The exclusion set is bounded.** It is cleared on every transition to SELECTING. It cannot grow unboundedly within a selection cycle because max_retries is finite.\n431\t\n432\t6. **Shutdown is always graceful when possible.** SIGTERM triggers STOPPED, not ERRORED. Only SIGKILL causes ungraceful termination, and heartbeat TTL handles that case.\n433\t\n434\t---\n435\t\n436\t# Architecture\n437\t\n438\t## Module Boundaries\n439\t\n440\tNEEDLE is organized into crates (Rust) or packages (Go) with strict dependency rules. No circular dependencies. Each module has a single responsibility.\n441\t\n442\t```\n443\tneedle (binary)\n444\t├── cli/              CLI parsing, session management\n445\t├── worker/           Worker loop, state machine\n446\t├── strand/           Strand waterfall evaluation\n447\t├── claim/            Atomic claiming, lock management\n448\t├── prompt/           Prompt construction from bead context\n449\t├── dispatch/         Agent adapter loading, process execution\n450\t├── outcome/          Exit code classification, outcome handlers\n451\t├── telemetry/        Structured event emission, sinks\n452\t├── health/           Heartbeat, stuck detection, peer monitoring\n453\t├── config/           Hierarchical configuration loading\n454\t├── bead_store/       Abstract bead backend interface\n455\t└── types/            Shared types, error definitions\n456\t```\n457\t\n458\t### Dependency Graph\n459\t\n460\t```\n461\tcli ──► worker ──► strand ──► bead_store\n462\t                │           │\n463\t                ├──► claim ─┘\n464\t                │\n465\t                ├──► prompt ──► bead_store\n466\t                │\n467\t                ├──► dispatch\n468\t                │\n469\t                ├──► outcome ──► bead_store\n470\t                │               ├──► telemetry\n471\t                │               └──► health\n472\t                │\n473\t                ├──► telemetry\n474\t                │\n475\t                └──► health ──► telemetry\n476\t\n477\tconfig ◄── (all modules)\n478\ttypes  ◄── (all modules)\n479\t```\n480\t\n481\t**Rule:** Arrows point from dependent to dependency. No module depends on `cli` or `worker` except through the binary entry point. `telemetry`, `config`, and `types` are leaf dependencies available to all modules.\n482\t\n483\t## Data Flow\n484\t\n485\t### Primary Loop\n486\t\n487\t```\n488\tbead_store ──[candidates]──► strand ──[bead_id]──► claim ──[claimed_bead]──►\n489\tprompt ──[prompt_string]──► dispatch ──[process]──► worker(wait) ──►\n490\toutcome ──[result]──► bead_store + telemetry\n491\t```\n492\t\n493\t### Telemetry Flow\n494\t\n495\t```\n496\t                    ┌─────────────────────────┐\n497\t                    │    Telemetry Collector   │\n498\t                    └────────────┬────────────┘\n499\t                                 │\n500\t              ┌──────────────────┼──────────────────┐\n501\t              ▼                  ▼                   ▼\n502\t        ┌──────────┐     ┌────────────┐      ┌──────────┐\n503\t        │ File Sink│     │ Stdout Sink│      │ Hook Sink│\n504\t        │ (JSONL)  │     │ (human)    │      │ (webhook)│\n505\t        └──────────┘     └────────────┘      └──────────┘\n506\t```\n507\t\n508\t### Configuration Flow\n509\t\n510\t```\n511\t  CLI args ──► env vars ──► workspace .needle.yaml ──► global ~/.needle/config.yaml ──► defaults\n512\t  (highest)                                                                              (lowest)\n513\t```\n514\t\n515\t## Module Specifications\n516\t\n517\t### bead_store\n518\t\n519\tAbstract interface to any bead backend. The primary implementation wraps the `br` CLI, but the trait allows future backends (direct SQLite, HTTP API, etc.).\n520\t\n521\t```\n522\ttrait BeadStore {\n523\t    fn ready(workspace: &Path, filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>>\n524\t    fn show(id: &BeadId) -> Result<Bead>\n525\t    fn claim(id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult>\n526\t    fn release(id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>\n527\t    fn labels(id: &BeadId) -> Result<Vec<String>>\n528\t    fn add_label(id: &BeadId, label: &str) -> Result<()>\n529\t    fn doctor_repair() -> Result<RepairReport>\n530\t}\n531\t\n532\tenum ClaimResult {\n533\t    Claimed(Bead),\n534\t    RaceLost { claimed_by: String },\n535\t    NotClaimable { reason: String },\n536\t}\n537\t```\n538\t\n539\t**Design notes:**\n540\t- All methods return `Result`. Silent failures do not exist.\n541\t- `ClaimResult` is an enum, not a boolean. The caller must handle each variant.\n542\t- `ready()` accepts filters (status, assignee, labels, workspace) to push filtering to the backend.\n543\t- The `br` CLI implementation shells out to `br` with `--json` and parses output via `serde_json`.\n544\t- JSON parsing failures are explicit errors, not empty results (learned from starvation false positives).\n545\t\n546\t### claim\n547\t\n548\tWraps `bead_store.claim()` with workspace-level serialization and retry logic.\n549\t\n550\t```\n551\tstruct Claimer {\n552\t    bead_store: Box<dyn BeadStore>,\n553\t    lock_dir: PathBuf,       // per-workspace flock directory\n554\t    max_retries: u32,        // default: 5\n555\t    retry_backoff_ms: u64,   // default: 100\n556\t}\n557\t\n558\timpl Claimer {\n559\t    fn claim_next(\n560\t        &self,\n561\t        candidates: &[Bead],\n562\t        actor: &str,\n563\t        exclusions: &HashSet<BeadId>,\n564\t    ) -> Result<ClaimOutcome>\n565\t}\n566\t\n567\tenum ClaimOutcome {\n568\t    Claimed(Bead),\n569\t    AllRaceLost,\n570\t    NoCandidates,\n571\t    StoreError(Error),\n572\t}\n573\t```\n574\t\n575\t**Design notes:**\n576\t- The flock is per-workspace, not per-bead. This serializes all claim operations within a workspace, preventing thundering herd (learned from `docs/notes/claim-race-conditions.md`).\n577\t- The lock is held only for the duration of the `br update --claim` call, not for the entire bead execution.\n578\t- Retry logic is internal to the Claimer. The caller receives a final `ClaimOutcome`.\n579\t\n580\t### strand\n581\t\n582\tEvaluates the strand waterfall and returns the next action.\n583\t\n584\t```\n585\ttrait Strand {\n586\t    fn name(&self) -> &str\n587\t    fn enabled(&self, config: &Config) -> bool\n588\t    fn evaluate(&self, context: &WorkerContext) -> Result<StrandResult>\n589\t}\n590\t\n591\tenum StrandResult {\n592\t    BeadFound(Vec<Bead>),    // candidates for claiming\n593\t    WorkCreated,              // strand created new beads (e.g., weave)\n594\t    NoWork,                   // fall through to next strand\n595\t    Error(StrandError),       // strand failed, fall through\n596\t}\n597\t```\n598\t\n599\tEach strand implements the trait. The runner evaluates them in order:\n600\t\n601\t```\n602\tfn run_strands(strands: &[Box<dyn Strand>], ctx: &WorkerContext) -> StrandWaterfallResult {\n603\t    for strand in strands {\n604\t        if !strand.enabled(&ctx.config) { continue; }\n605\t        match strand.evaluate(ctx)? {\n606\t            StrandResult::BeadFound(candidates) => return Ok(candidates),\n607\t            StrandResult::WorkCreated => return Ok(/* re-evaluate from strand 1 */),\n608\t            StrandResult::NoWork => continue,\n609\t            StrandResult::Error(e) => { emit_telemetry(e); continue; }\n610\t        }\n611\t    }\n612\t    StrandWaterfallResult::Exhausted\n613\t}\n614\t```\n615\t\n616\t### dispatch\n617\t\n618\tLoads agent adapters and executes the agent process.\n619\t\n620\t```\n621\tstruct Dispatcher {\n622\t    adapters: HashMap<String, AgentAdapter>,\n623\t}\n624\t\n625\tstruct AgentAdapter {\n626\t    name: String,\n627\t    invoke_template: String,   // e.g., \"cd {workspace} && claude --print\"\n628\t    input_method: InputMethod,  // Stdin, File, Args\n629\t    timeout: Duration,\n630\t    environment: HashMap<String, String>,\n631\t}\n632\t\n633\tenum InputMethod {\n634\t    Stdin,                      // pipe prompt to stdin\n635\t    File { path_template: String },  // write prompt to file, pass path\n636\t    Args { flag: String },      // pass prompt as --flag value\n637\t}\n638\t\n639\tstruct ExecutionResult {\n640\t    exit_code: i32,\n641\t    stdout: String,\n642\t    stderr: String,\n643\t    elapsed: Duration,\n644\t    pid: u32,\n645\t}\n646\t```\n647\t\n648\t**Design notes:**\n649\t- Adapters are loaded from YAML config files. Adding a new agent requires only a new YAML file.\n650\t- The invoke template is rendered with variables: `{workspace}`, `{prompt_file}`, `{bead_id}`, `{model}`.\n651\t- The dispatcher does not interpret agent output. It captures raw exit code, stdout, and stderr, then passes them to the outcome handler.\n652\t- Timeout is enforced by the dispatcher, not the agent.
